title: Renewal Rescue — Scenario Runbook & Constructive Review Template
body:
Purpose:
This runbook is a practical template to guide rapid renewal-rescue activity and a post-loss constructive review for accounts at risk of churn. It combines a rapid triage checklist for on-the-ground CS/Renewal reps, a structured timeline to reconstruct events, a counterfactual scenario matrix (what we could've changed), and a reproducible set of next steps for re-engagement or internal remediation.

Scope:
- Intended for mid-market and enterprise accounts where a renewal was downgraded, delayed, or lost.
- Combines customer-facing rescue steps + internal after-action review (AAR).
- Not a legal or finance instrument; finance/sales follow existing contract handoffs.

How to use this doc:
1) Copy into account-specific folder (name file: [ACCT]-renewal-rescue-[YYYYMMDD]).
2) Fill the Quick Triage block immediately when a risk signal appears.
3) Run Rescue play within 48 hours if there is a reasonable path to renewal (intake, exec sponsor outreach, mitigation plan).
4) If renewal is lost, switch to Post-loss AAR timeline and follow the Counterfactual matrix.

Quick triage (first 48h) — checklist for the acting CS/AE:
- [ ] Signal source: (billing, product gap, price, competitor, org change) — note primary and secondary reasons.
- [ ] Customer health snapshot: last NPS, usage trend (30/90/180d), error rates, outstanding tickets.
- [ ] Contract dates: renewal date, auto-renew window, notice requirement.
- [ ] Stakeholder map: primary champion, economic buyer, technical decision-maker, new stakeholders.
- [ ] Open blockers: top 3 product/ops issues and their owners.
- [ ] Proposed immediate remedy (owner + ETA).
- [ ] Exec contact plan (who, when, channel).

Rescue play options (pick 1–3 and execute):
- Executive Sponsor Pulse: 30-min call between our VP/GM and the customer's econ buyer to reset value framing.
- Technical Deep-dive: 90-min session with product/SE to address integration/perf gaps and produce a remediation ticket with SLA.
- Commercial Flex: limited extension, pilot reframe, or short-term discount tied to roadmap milestones (must involve RevOps approval).
- Service Augmentation: temporary increase in support hours or dedicated delivery resource for migration.

Decision matrix — continue rescue vs. accept loss:
- Likelihood to succeed (Low/Medium/High) based on adoption trend + sponsor strength.
- Cost to execute (Low/Med/High) measured in dedicated SE time + discount.
- Strategic value (strategic/expansion/reference/non-strategic).
If (Likelihood*Strategic) > Cost (team judgment), pursue rescue; otherwise prioritize AAR to recover learnings.

Post-loss Constructive Review (AAR) — timeline template to reconstruct events:
- Day 0 — Loss confirmed: record who delivered the notice and the exact wording. Capture customer communication thread (screenshot/quotes).
- Day 1–3 — Evidence collection: usage logs, ticket history, meeting notes, contract and renewal cadence, pricing changes. Tag relevant Jira tickets.
- Day 3–7 — Internal interviews: CS lead, AE, SE, Product manager, Support manager, Billing owner. Use the Interview Guide (below).
- Day 7–10 — Draft AAR: timeline, root cause analysis, counterfactuals, recommended fixes. Circulate to stakeholders.
- Day 10–14 — Finalize AAR and assign owners for remediation actions. Add remediation items to team backlog and track in sprint.

Interview guide (questions for internal stakeholders):
- What signals did we miss or misinterpret?
- When did the customer's intent shift and why?
- Which handoffs were friction points? (date and owner)
- Were there product limitations; were workarounds proposed?
- Pricing/contract issues: were they raised early? Were alternatives offered?
- Is there an immediate path to re-engage in 90 days? 6 months?

Root cause categories (pick all that apply and add evidence):
- Product maturity/feature gap (describe feature + impact).
- Performance/scale or reliability incident(s) (link logs/incidents).
- Commercial mismatch (pricing, packaging, contract inflexibility).
- Org changes on customer side (procurement, leadership churn).
- Implementation/enablement failure (onboarding, training, CSM bandwidth).
- Competitive displacement (who, offer, why).
- Support experience failure (SLA breach, escalations).

Counterfactual scenario matrix (example rows — fill columns):
Columns: Scenario ID | What we would have done differently | Who would have to act | Feasible? (Y/N) | Estimated impact on outcome | Effort to implement (Low/Med/High)
- Scenario 1 | Earlier exec escalation at 30% usage drop | CSM + AE + GM | Y | High | Low
- Scenario 2 | Temporary rebate linked to delivery milestones | RevOps + AE | Y | Medium | Medium
- Scenario 3 | Fast-track engineering fix in 2 weeks | Eng + Product + SE | N (resource constraints) | High | High

Re-engagement playbook (if re-opened conversation):
- Wait period: minimum cooling period (recommended 30 days) unless customer asks to engage sooner.
- Re-contact owner: CRO/Head of CS with a single clear ask (e.g., a facts-only audit + proposal).
- Offer: limited-scope remediation + time-boxed proof-of-value (PoV) with acceptance criteria and success metrics.
- Internal commitment: executive sponsor and SE assigned; timeline published.

Metrics & artifacts to attach (must include links):
- Usage trends CSV (30/90/180 days)
- Support ticket export (last 180 days)
- NPS/CSAT history for account
- Meeting notes (link) and call recordings (link)
- Contract & pricing history snapshot

Communication templates (short snippets):
- Exec outreach subject: "Proposal to stabilize [ACCT] relationship — 30-min"
- Customer email (if re-opening): "Hi [Name], we reviewed what happened and have a focused plan to address the issues you raised. Can we schedule 30 minutes to review a time-boxed proposal?"
- Internal summary to leadership: 3 bullets (1) root cause, (2) counterfactual with highest impact, (3) recommended next action + owner + ETA.

Ownership & tracking:
- AAR owner (name): [AAR_OWNER]
- Rescue owner (name): [RESCUE_OWNER]
- Follow-up cadence: weekly until actions closed, then monthly check-ins for 3 months.

Knowledge capture & product feedback loop:
- Tag product PRD or roadmap items that were implicated.
- Create a short "customer story" (1–2 paragraphs) for product and sales training.
- If issue is systemic, propose a cross-functional remediation epic and link to engineering backlog.

Post-AAR retrospective questions for team learning:
- What early warning signals will we add to our health scoring?
- Which handoff steps will be standardized to avoid recurrence?
- Is there a repeatable rescue play that should be codified into an SLO or process?

Appendix — Quick fillable fields (paste at top of account copy):
- Account name: [ACCOUNT NAME]
- ARR at risk: [ARR]
- Renewal date: [YYYY-MM-DD]
- Primary reason given by customer: [SHORT_REASON]
- Primary sponsor (customer): [NAME + ROLE]
- CSM: [NAME]
- AE: [NAME]
- SE (if any): [NAME]
- AAR owner (internal): [NAME]
- Tags: [e.g., implementation, price, reliability]

Notes & iteration history:
- 2024-11-06 — initial draft (Maya Patel).
- 2024-12-10 — added counterfactual matrix and interview guide (Liam Chen).

End of template.

Quick reminder: this doc is meant to be actionable and lightweight — prefer filling evidence links and short bullets to long essays. If the opportunity is strategic, escalate to the CS leadership review channel and pull in product/eng early.
